quests.prompt: Keeping a pet dog is good for a family.
options: Dogs offer loyal companionship and reduce feelings of loneliness.

Dogs need constant care, which takes a lot of time and energy.
Walking a dog encourages the whole family to exercise every day.
quests.hint: Think about what dogs give to a family (Pros) and what they cost (Cons).
quests.explanation: Dogs provide companionship and encourage exercise (Pros), but they are costly and time-consuming to look after (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

Parents often end up doing most of the pet care themselves.
Caring for a dog helps children develop empathy and kindness.
quests.hint: Consider what children gain from caring for a dog (Pros) and the challenges involved (Cons).
quests.explanation: Dog ownership builds responsibility and empathy in children (Pros), but young children may lack maturity, leaving parents to do most of the work (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).
quests.prompt: Pet dogs make the home a safer and more enjoyable place.

Dogs can alert the family to strangers and act as natural home protectors.
The presence of a dog creates a warm and lively atmosphere at home.
quests.hint: Think about what dogs add to home life (Pros) and the problems they can cause (Cons).
quests.explanation: Dogs improve home security and atmosphere (Pros), but they can trigger allergies and create mess that is difficult to manage (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

quests.hint: Think about how breakfast helps children at school (Pros) and what makes it difficult (Cons).
quests.explanation: Breakfast improves energy and school performance (Pros), but some children dislike eating early, and preparation adds pressure to busy mornings (Cons).

Breakfast boosts metabolism and helps people maintain a healthy body weight.
Morning meals provide essential vitamins and minerals the body needs.
quests.hint: Consider the health benefits of breakfast (Pros) and situations where it may not help (Cons).
quests.explanation: Breakfast supports metabolism and nutrition (Pros), but poor food choices or medically supervised fasting can make regular breakfast less suitable (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

options: Starting the day with a meal creates a calm and positive morning routine.
Rushed mornings often make sitting down for a meal completely impractical.
Eating too early can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.
Breakfast time gives family members a chance to sit and talk together.
quests.hint: Think about what a breakfast routine adds to family life (Pros) and when it is difficult (Cons).
quests.explanation: A breakfast routine encourages calmness and family communication (Pros), but busy schedules and digestive sensitivity can make it hard to maintain (Cons).

Active travel helps children arrive at school feeling alert and ready to learn.
Children who live far from school cannot easily walk or cycle safely.
Bad weather such as heavy rain or snow makes active travel unpleasant and difficult.
quests.hint: Think about the benefits of walking or cycling to school (Pros) and the barriers (Cons).
quests.explanation: Active travel boosts fitness and alertness (Pros), but distance and weather can make it impractical or unsafe for many children (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).
quests.prompt: Walking or cycling to school is better for the environment.
options: Parents of young children often feel it is unsafe to let them travel alone.
Active travel produces no exhaust emissions, reducing local air pollution.
Not all routes between home and school have safe pavements or cycle paths.
Fewer cars on the school run means less traffic congestion around schools.
quests.hint: Consider the environmental benefits (Pros) and the safety concerns (Cons).
quests.explanation: Walking and cycling cut pollution and reduce traffic (Pros), but safety concerns and the lack of safe routes make many parents reluctant (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).
quests.prompt: Encouraging active travel to school builds children's independence.
options: Walking or cycling alone helps children develop confidence and self-reliance.
Independent travel teaches children to navigate their local area responsibly.
Younger primary school children may genuinely not be safe travelling alone.
Parents may worry excessively, causing stress even when the journey is safe.
quests.hint: Think about what active travel teaches children (Pros) and what concerns parents (Cons).
quests.explanation: Independent travel builds confidence and navigation skills (Pros), but younger children may lack the maturity for solo travel, and parental anxiety can be a significant barrier (Cons).

Children who read for pleasure tend to have better writing and comprehension skills.

Busy school schedules leave little free time for children to read casually.
quests.hint: Think about what reading gives children (Pros) and what stops them reading (Cons).
quests.explanation: Reading builds vocabulary and literacy skills (Pros), but some children find it unappealing, and heavy school workloads can crowd out leisure reading (Cons).

Stories introduce children to new worlds, ideas, and perspectives.
Engaging with fictional characters helps children understand different emotions.
Passive screen entertainment can feel more immediately rewarding than reading.
quests.hint: Consider what fiction reading develops in children (Pros) and what concerns parents (Cons).
quests.explanation: Fiction reading builds imagination and emotional intelligence (Pros), but some parents prefer factual reading, and screens offer more instant entertainment (Cons).

Getting lost in a story can reduce anxiety and improve children's mood.
quests.hint: Think about the wellbeing benefits of reading (Pros) and when it might not help (Cons).
quests.explanation: Reading reduces stress and improves mood (Pros), but it can feel isolating, and children who struggle with reading may find it stressful rather than calming (Cons).

Social events and family activities sometimes make an early bedtime impossible.
A consistent bedtime ensures children get the recommended hours of sleep.
Regular sleep patterns improve children's concentration and behaviour at school.
quests.hint: Think about the benefits of a regular bedtime (Pros) and the challenges of keeping it (Cons).

Adequate sleep strengthens the immune system, helping children fight illness.

quests.hint: Consider how early sleep benefits children's bodies (Pros) and when it becomes problematic (Cons).
quests.explanation: Sleep supports physical growth and immunity (Pros), but teenagers have a naturally later sleep rhythm, making very early bedtimes counterproductive for older children (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

options: A predictable evening routine helps younger children feel secure and calm.
Having a set bedtime gives parents quiet time to rest and recharge in the evening.
Children often resist bedtime routines, making evenings stressful for parents.
Different children in the same family may need different bedtimes, making routine harder.
quests.hint: Think about what a bedtime routine gives the family (Pros) and what difficulties it brings (Cons).
quests.explanation: Bedtime routines create security for children and recovery time for parents (Pros), but resistance from children and differing needs within the family can make them stressful to maintain (Cons).

options: Vegetables provide essential vitamins and minerals that support healthy growth.
A diet rich in vegetables reduces the risk of serious diseases later in life.

quests.explanation: Vegetables supply vital nutrients and protect long-term health (Pros), but children's resistance to eating them and the preparation time required can make this a daily challenge (Cons).

Vegetables contain complex carbohydrates that provide sustained energy throughout the day.
Forcing children to eat foods they dislike can create negative feelings around mealtimes.
Key nutrients in vegetables support healthy brain function and learning ability.
quests.hint: Consider how vegetables affect children's energy and learning (Pros) and the downsides of enforcement (Cons).
quests.explanation: Vegetables sustain energy and support learning (Pros), but children's preference for convenient processed food and the risk of creating food anxiety make strict enforcement problematic (Cons).

options: Children raised with strict food rules sometimes rebel against healthy eating as teenagers.
Children who eat well early in life are more likely to maintain healthy diets as adults.
Individual food preferences and cultural diets mean universal vegetable rules are not practical.
Regular vegetable eating from a young age normalises healthy food choices.
quests.hint: Think about the long-term habits vegetables can build (Pros) and when strict rules may backfire (Cons).
quests.explanation: Early healthy eating habits tend to last into adulthood (Pros), but overly strict rules can trigger teenage rebellion against healthy food, and cultural variation makes universal rules impractical (Cons).

quests.hint: Think about what cooking teaches children (Pros) and what concerns parents (Cons).

Some teenagers lack interest in cooking and prefer quicker, ready-made meal options.
People who cook their own food tend to eat fewer processed and fast food meals.
Understanding ingredients helps young people make informed nutritional decisions.
quests.hint: Consider how home cooking affects young people's diets (Pros) and the practical barriers (Cons).

Preparing meals together gives families quality time and a shared activity.
Kitchen disagreements about methods or meals can cause more conflict than connection.
Cooking with parents teaches children practical skills in a relaxed and natural way.
quests.hint: Think about how cooking together benefits families (Pros) and when it causes problems (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

Playing with other children builds crucial social skills and teamwork abilities.
Busy roads and urban environments make outdoor play genuinely dangerous for some children.
Cold, wet, or extreme weather makes outdoor play uncomfortable or even unsafe.
quests.hint: Think about what outdoor play gives children (Pros) and the safety concerns (Cons).
quests.explanation: Outdoor play builds physical fitness and social skills (Pros), but traffic dangers and poor weather make it difficult or unsafe in many locations and seasons (Cons).

Unstructured outdoor play encourages creativity and independent thinking.
Some children prefer indoor activities and should not be forced outside against their will.
Excessive sun exposure without protection carries real health risks for children.
quests.hint: Consider the mental health benefits of outdoor play (Pros) and when it may not be appropriate (Cons).

options: Many children live in cities where access to green spaces and nature is very limited.
Time in nature builds environmental awareness and appreciation from an early age.
Screen-based entertainment is increasingly more appealing to children than outdoor activities.
Outdoor experiences encourage curiosity and a love of learning about the world.
quests.hint: Think about what outdoor play in nature teaches children (Pros) and what limits access to it (Cons).
quests.explanation: Nature play builds environmental awareness and curiosity (Pros), but limited access to green spaces in cities and the pull of digital entertainment reduce opportunities for many children (Cons).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

quests.instruction: Decide if each statement is a Pro (it supports the opinion) or a Con (it argues against it).

Establishing and maintaining a family routine requires sustained effort and consistent discipline.

Shared routines help family members coordinate and support each other more effectively.

quests.explanation: Shared routines reduce conflict and help families coordinate effectively (Pros), but maintaining them requires effort and real-world disruptions frequently undermine even the best-laid schedules (Cons).
